name: Disorder of Glyoxylate Metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glyoxylate Metabolism Disorder

criteria.description: Persistent elevated glyoxylate levels in plasma or urine
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in glyoxylate metabolism (e.g., AGXT, GRHPR, HOGA1)
Presence of clinical manifestations such as recurrent nephrolithiasis or oxalate nephropathy
Renal biopsy showing calcium oxalate crystal deposition

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated glyoxylate levels plus pathogenic genetic mutation and clinical features consistent with glyoxylate metabolism disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; biochemical assays support diagnosis.

searchTerms: repeated kidney stones made of calcium oxalate

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary hyperoxaluria with systemic oxalate deposition
searchTerms: excess oxalate causing deposits throughout body
calcium deposits in kidneys seen on scan

common.symptomName: Renal insufficiency or chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: kidney failure or reduced kidney function
failure to gain weight as expected

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to oxalate deposition
searchTerms: aching bones due to oxalate buildup
painful bones caused by crystal accumulation

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to systemic oxalosis
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to crystal deposits
hard skin spots from crystal accumulation

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms from oxalate deposition in CNS
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from oxalate in brain
neurological problems due to crystal deposits
brain and nerve issues from oxalate

rare.symptomName: Retinal oxalate crystal deposition causing visual impairment
searchTerms: eye damage caused by crystal deposits

rare.symptomName: Systemic oxalosis leading to multi-organ failure
searchTerms: organ damage due to systemic crystal buildup
failure of multiple organs from oxalosis

laboratory: Elevated plasma and urinary glyoxylate and oxalate levels
Elevated serum creatinine in renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis and nephrolithiasis
Bone radiographs showing oxalate crystal deposition
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in AGXT gene (primary hyperoxaluria type 1)
Mutations in GRHPR gene (primary hyperoxaluria type 2)
Mutations in HOGA1 gene (primary hyperoxaluria type 3)
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating calcium oxalate crystal deposition
Histopathological evidence of systemic oxalosis in advanced disease

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with more severe renal involvement
Milder clinical course compared to type 1
Due to increased dietary oxalate or intestinal absorption
No genetic mutations in glyoxylate metabolism genes

redFlags: Early onset recurrent nephrolithiasis in infancy or childhood
Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease
Systemic oxalate deposition causing multi-organ dysfunction
references: Hoppe B, et al. Primary hyperoxaluria. N Engl J Med. 2020;382(3):234-244.
